gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Nebula's own support page says Netflix on the Mars 3 is a mobile build installed through the Nebula Play app and controlled only in mouse mode from the phone app, while Nebula's spec sheets list both the Nebula X1 and the Cosmos 4K SE as 'Google TV with Official Netflix'.
standout_why: Wirecutter's best-projectors page, which ChatGPT cited, already says of its outdoor pick, the Mars 3, 'you do have to sideload Netflix', so the main limit is partly known. It does not say the build is a mobile version that can only be driven in mouse mode from the phone. It also doesn't contrast the Mars 3 with the X1 or Cosmos 4K SE, which ship official Netflix, and mentions no power station for any pick. ChatGPT's own answer only says the X1 'Requires AC power', with no adapter rating or power-station pairing. I could not compare against the RTINGS outdoor list or the RTINGS X1 review (both came back as navigation menus only), Yahoo Tech (HTTP 403) or Forbes Vetted (redirect not followed), so I can't rule out that one of those covers part of this.
decides: ChatGPT called the Mars 3 the best battery-powered pick, but it has no official Netflix TV app; Nebula's workaround is a phone-controlled mobile build. Shoppers who want a smart projector that just streams Netflix should pick the X1 or the Cosmos 4K SE (both Google TV with official Netflix) and add a power station where there's no outlet. Notebookcheck says 'even a compact power station with 500 Wh is therefore sufficient for most movie nights outdoors'. The Mars 3 stays the pick only if built-in battery runtime matters more than native Netflix, or if the buyer adds a streaming stick over HDMI.

findings.label: How Netflix works
findings.value: A mobile version of Netflix installed through the Nebula Play app (Google Play Store > Nebula Play > Tips > Netflix Installation); 'it can only be controlled in mouse mode' with the Anker Nebula phone app
findings.source_title: How to install and use Netflix on Capsule 3 Laser/Mars 3? (soundcore support)
findings.note: Maker support article. The title covers Capsule 3 Laser and Mars 3. It says to update the firmware first, and it does not call this the official Netflix TV app.

findings.label: OS and Netflix on the maker's product page
findings.value: The FAQ says 'Mars 3 comes with the Android TV system' and has you install Netflix from the Nebula Play app; the page also says 'Compatible with Android TV 11.0'
findings.source_title: soundcore Nebula Mars 3 | Outdoor Projector with 5H Long Playtime
findings.note: The spec list on the same page says 'Google TV', which contradicts the FAQ. The FAQ and support article agree on Android TV with Netflix through Nebula Play.

findings.label: Battery, power input, water resistance
findings.value: 185 Wh battery; 5 h of video in Eco Mode; power adapter rated 19 V / 9.47 A (about 180 W); IPX3
findings.source_title: soundcore Nebula Mars 3 | Outdoor Projector with 5H Long Playtime
findings.note: 19 × 9.47 = 179.9 W is my arithmetic. The page lists no car charging, no USB-C power input and no power-station compatibility.

findings.label: Adapter rating and US store price
findings.source_title: soundcore NEBULA X1 4K Triple Laser Projector (US store)
findings.note: 22 × 10.9 = 239.8 W is my arithmetic. The page says the X1 is 'Designed for both home theater setups and outdoor viewing' and gives no water rating. It lists the satellite speakers, mics and carry case as X1 bundle add-ons. The $2,999.00 was the listed price on the fetched page, but I could not tell whether a bundle was selected, so ChatGPT's $1,899.00 card price is unverified.

findings.label: Measured power draw and power-station pairing (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: About 160 at maximum brightness (published as 'Wh'); 'a good 0.3 kWh' for a two-hour movie; 'Even a compact power station with 500 Wh is therefore sufficient for most movie nights outdoors'
findings.source_title: Impressive 4K laser projector with optional 4.1.2 sound: Nebula X1 in a practical test (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Notebookcheck printed '160 Wh', which is most likely watts. Arithmetic from its figure: 0.3 kWh per 2-hour movie is about 150 W on average, so a 1,024 Wh station such as the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 or EcoFlow DELTA 3 would cover about three movies before inverter losses. That estimate is mine, not a maker claim.
